page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by KVM virtualization. The instance features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 62 GB of system RAM, providing approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture, paired with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance carries a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark results reflect the specialization of the underlying hardware. In general CPU tasks, single-thread performance is modest, registering weak scores across stress-ng (1110.08) and Geekbench (937.0). Multi-core benchmarks sit in the average bracket, with Geekbench multi-core reaching 5951.0 and PassMark CPU reaching 13056.17. Synthetic memory tests indicate moderate throughput, with read bandwidth measuring 73.63 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 53.83 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks. Where the instance demonstrates peak efficiency is in Tensor Core accelerated inference. The integrated NVIDIA T4 achieves top-tier throughput in prompt processing for both 135M (8410.67 tokens/sec) and 7B (1141.42 tokens/sec) language models, alongside strong text generation throughput of 34.57 tokens/sec on the 7B model.

In terms of resource balance and cost efficiency, the ecs.gn6i-c16g1.4xlarge provides an economical entry point for machine learning inference without the hardware expense associated with high-end training GPUs. The primary operational tradeoffs involve lower single-core execution speed and reliance on external network volumes for storage IOPS. This profile is best suited for small to medium scale machine learning model inference, video transcoding, visual computing, and lightweight distributed AI workloads.

It operates on the KVM hypervisor with 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and requires remote storage volumes due to the absence of local disks. Benchmark evaluations reveal moderate general CPU performance, with multi-core throughput reaching the middle tier. In contrast, the NVIDIA T4 delivers exceptional prompt processing speeds for language models up to 7B parameters, placing it in the top tier of inference efficiency. The hardware profile represents a cost-effective platform tailored specifically for AI inference pipelines, video processing, and GPU-driven analytical workloads.
